title: TinyStroke Creator Brief
summary: Everything you need to film a TinyStroke video that sells: every winning ad as a moving preview, the two to recreate shot by shot, ready-to-use scripts, and how to deliver.
previewNote: Private preview. Rose reviews this before it goes to creators.

welcome.heading: Welcome
welcome.body: Thanks for creating with TinyStroke! We're a small family brand, and our best ads all look like a real parent filming on their phone at home, not like a commercial. This page shows you exactly what has worked for us so you can make something that works for you too.
welcome.oneLine: Show a real parent proving, on camera, that these crayons don't break, show up bright, and wipe right off the wall.

facts.label: Twist-up
facts.value: No sharpening, no snapping, no paper to peel

facts.label: Washable
facts.value: Wipes off walls, cabinets, clothes and surfaces with a wet cloth

facts.label: Grip
facts.value: Chunky shape made for little hands

facts.label: Comes in
facts.value: A sturdy tub-style case to store them

filming.heading: What we're looking for
items: Vertical 9:16, filmed handheld on your phone (iPhone-style), not a tripod studio setup.
Candid and real: your own kitchen, table, wall or playroom. A little mess is good.
Voice-led: you talking to camera or a voiceover carries the video. No background music needed.
Bright, natural light (near a window) so the colors pop on camera.
Real use: your child coloring, or your hands showing the crayons up close.
Proof on camera: twist it, try to snap it, scribble on a wall and wipe it off in one take.
Short and fast: 15 to 45 seconds, a new shot every 2 to 3 seconds.

heroes.heading: Hero ad 1: Why your toddler doesn't like to draw
heroes.caption: 31 seconds, creator on camera in her kitchen.
heroes.libraryLabel: Open hero ad 1 in the Meta Ad Library
shots: Close-up: regular crayon held right at the lens. Text: pov: your toddler finally wants to color
This is why your toddler doesn't want to color.
Notebook: faint regular-crayon scribble next to a bold silky one
You can barely see it… look how much more vibrant that is.
Twists and pushes on the crayon
Toddlers are always doing this. You literally cannot break them, no matter how hard you try.
Talking to camera, crayon in hand
Twistable, non-toxic, and they're washable.
Scribbles on her white cabinet, wipes it with a wet washcloth
You didn't believe me? Here's my white cabinet… here's my wet washcloth. It comes right off.
Holds the tub up to camera
They come in this nice case. The 36 count is the only pack left because they keep selling out. I would hurry.
heroes.why: Why it works: it names the parent's real problem (my kid won't color) and blames the crayon, not the child. The live wipe test on a white cabinet is the moment that sells.

heroes.heading: Hero ad 2: Toddler-proof crayons
heroes.caption: 38 seconds, voiceover over hands-only footage.
heroes.libraryLabel: Open hero ad 2 in the Meta Ad Library
shots: Hand holds a cup of ordinary crayons. Text: Toddler proof crayons exist. I am shocked too.
How dare they reinvent the crayon?
The 36 tub, then both sets side by side on a coloring page
There are three reasons why these are so much more popular than these.
Twisting a crayon up, pile of crayons on the table
Number one: they don't snap in half.
Coloring page split in half: regular crayon vs silky crayon
See how this is the color of the crayon? Look how much more vibrant… and so much smoother.
Scribble on the tub or surface, wipe with a damp tissue
These are washable.
Coloring cute pages (donut, pickles), squiggle lines
Three of the four pack options are sold out. Don't mess up like me: I got the 6 pack, then had to get the 36.
Full tub, lid on, arrow pointing down
Don't miss these, they're 50% off right now.
heroes.why: Why it works: a bold claim plus surprise in the first second, a numbered list that keeps people watching, a side-by-side comparison you can't argue with, and a personal "I upgraded" story before the offer.

gallery.heading: All winning ads
gallery.caption: Every ad from our winning-creatives list, grouped by pattern. Each card plays in place with sound. Notes are from the actual footage.
gallery.intro: Scroll through these before you film. Pick the pattern that fits your home and style, then use the matching script template below.

groups.heading: Pattern 1: "They can't see the color" side-by-side
groups.intro: The most common winner. Old crayon vs silky crayon on the same notepad, then a break test and a wipe.

ads.title: American vs UK crayon (hands only)
ads.hook: Text: pov your toddler WANTS to color now. Says: "American crayon versus the British crayon."
ads.scene: Notepad comparison, push test, scribble on a white cabinet and wipe, ends writing HURRY
ads.why: Same script as hero 1, but hands only: proves the script works without a face on camera
ads.note: Listed twice in the sheet (rows 2 and 11).

ads.title: American vs British crayon (kitchen)
ads.hook: Text: American vs British crayon. Says: "What's the difference between American crayons and British crayons?"
ads.scene: Talking to camera at the kitchen counter, notepad, break test, wall scribble wiped with a wet rag
ads.why: A curiosity question as the hook, plus a tantrum pain point and the wall test

ads.title: This is bad, but this is good
ads.hook: Text: pov: this is why your toddler doesn't want to color. Says: "This is bad, but this is good" (repeated)
ads.scene: Male creator, notepad comparison, wall scribble, close-up of the open tub
ads.why: A rhythmic repeated line stops the scroll; adds the money angle (no more rebuying crayons)

ads.title: Screen-free + mess-free
ads.hook: Text: screen + mess free = mom wins. Says: "This is why your toddler doesn't like to draw."
ads.scene: Kitchen counter, regular crayons vs silky on a notepad, push test, wipe with a cloth

ads.title: Your child can't see these crayons
ads.hook: Says: "Your child can't see these crayons."
ads.scene: Male creator, faint vs bold scribble on paper, crayon to camera, wipe, tub to lens

ads.scene: Male creator, orange crayon vs silky on notepad, break test, wipe on a book, tub

ads.scene: Hands only on white paper: regular vs silky lines, twist, wipe off a hand, the 36 tub

ads.scene: Talking to camera with the open tub, notepad comparisons, snap test, wall scribble wiped with a paper towel

groups.heading: Pattern 2: Hands-only demo (no face)
groups.intro: Tabletop footage with a voiceover or captions. Easy to film and easy to remix.

ads.title: Toddler-proof crayons (cut 2)

groups.heading: Pattern 3: Wall, door and cabinet wipe

ads.title: Yes, I'm that mom

shared.heading: What all our winners share
shared.caption: Main pattern across the 21 different videos in our winning-creatives list, including the two heroes
points: The hook blames old crayons, not the child: "this is why your toddler doesn't want to color".
Proof beats claims: side-by-side color, a twist-and-push break test, and a wipe test, all on camera.
Nearly every ad shows a wipe test: wall, door, cabinet, tray or hand.
Three benefits in this order: unbreakable, vibrant and smooth, washable. Non-toxic is a quick add.
One short text line on screen in the first second, usually a POV line.
Every ad ends on scarcity or an offer: packs keep selling out, it's on sale, don't wait.

scripts.heading: Script templates
scripts.intro: Use these as a starting point and say them in your own words. Film each hook as a separate take so we can test them.

items.title: A. Toddler-proof, 3 reasons (from hero ad 2)
items.body:
HOOK (0-3s)
Text on screen: Toddler proof crayons exist. I am shocked too.
Say: "How dare they reinvent the crayon?"

BODY (3-28s)
"There are three reasons these are so much better than these."
1. Try to snap one, twist it up: "They don't break, they don't snap in half."
2. Color half a page with each: "Look how much more vibrant and smooth these are."
3. Scribble on a surface, wipe it off: "And they're washable."

CTA (28-38s)
"I first got a small pack and had to go back for the 36 because they're that good.
They keep selling out and they're on sale right now, so don't wait."

items.title: B. Why your toddler doesn't like to draw (from hero ad 1)
items.body:
HOOK (0-3s)
Text on screen: pov: your toddler finally wants to color
Hold a regular crayon right up to the lens.
Say: "This is why your toddler doesn't want to color."

BODY (3-24s)
Scribble with both in a notebook: "They can barely see it. Look how much brighter this is."
Push and twist hard: "Toddlers are always doing this. You cannot break these."
"Twistable, non-toxic, and washable. Don't believe me?"
Scribble on a white cabinet or wall, wipe with a wet cloth: "Comes right off."

CTA (24-31s)
Hold up the tub: "They come in this nice case. They keep selling out, so I would hurry."

items.title: C. Yes, I'm that mom (wall test)
items.body:
HOOK (0-3s)
Text on screen: pov: your toddler finally wants to color
Scribble on a white door or wall. Say: "Yes, I'm that mom that lets her kids color all over the walls."

BODY (3-28s)
"And no, I don't freak out, because I only buy these silky crayons."
Notepad: "Old crayons, you can barely see that. New silky crayons."
Snap test: "Old crayons break just like that. Silky crayons do not break."
Wipe the wall in one take: "All it takes is one baby wipe."

CTA (28-35s)
"They've sold out a few times, but they just restocked. Grab them before they sell out again."

dos.heading: Do's and don'ts
dos: Film in natural daylight so colors look bright
Show the wipe test in one continuous take
Put a regular crayon next to ours for comparison
Keep the camera close: hands, crayon tips, the page
Talk like you're telling a friend, not reading
Leave 1 second of silence at the start and end of each clip
donts: No background music, filters or heavy effects
No horizontal video or studio lighting
Don't name or show other crayon brands
Don't promise discounts or prices we didn't confirm
Don't leave a child unattended with the crayons on camera
dos.claims: Stick to the claims in our winning ads: twistable, doesn't snap, washable, non-toxic, vibrant colors. Any wording on age suitability or safety certifications is to be confirmed by Rose.

steps.detail: Use one of the script templates and record 3 hook takes.

steps.title: Upload everything to one folder

steps.title: Send us the link

steps.title: Feedback and revisions
